title: True or False: A Product Owner can solely decide to release an Increment to the market without consulting the Developers. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to ensure the Increment meets the Definition of Done before release. Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The release decision should consider the readiness of the Increment as defined by the team.
explanation2: Correct: Releasing an Increment should be a collaborative decision involving both the Product Owner and Developers.

title: A critical bug is discovered mid-Sprint that impacts the product’s core functionality. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to address critical bugs immediately to maintain product quality and stakeholder confidence. “Developers are responsible for turning Product Backlog items into Increments of value each Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Wait until the next Sprint to address the bug.
explanation1: Incorrect: Critical bugs impacting core functionality should be addressed immediately.
answer2: Work with the Developers to address the bug within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing critical issues promptly ensures the product remains functional and reliable.
answer3: Defer the bug fix to a later release if the team is busy.
explanation3: Incorrect: Deferring a critical fix can lead to greater risks and stakeholder dissatisfaction.
answer4: Reassign the bug fix to a separate team to avoid disrupting the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing work across separate teams can lead to communication issues and inconsistency.

title: The Developers are consistently not meeting the Definition of Done for completed items. What is the first step the Product Owner should take? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to understand and address issues related to the Definition of Done, ensuring that quality standards are consistently met. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adjust the Definition of Done to match the team’s current capabilities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering the Definition of Done undermines the quality standards of the product.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to understand why they are struggling to meet the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Identifying and addressing the root causes helps improve adherence to quality standards.
answer3: Remove incomplete items from the Product Backlog to reduce the workload.
explanation3: Incorrect: Removing items without addressing the underlying issues does not solve the problem.
answer4: Ignore the issue and focus on getting more items done.
explanation4: Incorrect: Focusing on quantity over quality compromises the product’s value and integrity.

title: Which two actions help ensure that the Development Team adheres to the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Adhering to the Definition of Done involves regularly reviewing it during refinement and using it as a guideline to ensure quality throughout the development process. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Conducting regular reviews of the Definition of Done during Backlog Refinement sessions.
explanation1: Correct: Reviewing the Definition of Done helps ensure it remains relevant and that the team consistently applies it.
answer2: Incorporating the Definition of Done as a checklist during development and testing.
explanation2: Correct: Using the Definition of Done as a checklist helps the team maintain focus on quality and completeness.
answer3: Allowing the Product Owner to approve work before it is marked done.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done defines when work is complete; it is not based on Product Owner approval.
answer4: Revising the Definition of Done whenever work becomes too challenging.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should not be compromised for convenience; it is a standard of quality.
answer5: Skipping Retrospectives if work meets the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: Retrospectives are essential for continuous improvement and should not be skipped, regardless of the outcome.

title: Which three practices help maintain high transparency in the Scrum Team’s work? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining transparency involves regularly updating the Product Backlog, conducting Sprint Reviews, and using tools like Task Boards to visualize progress. “Scrum’s artifacts represent work or value and are designed to maximize transparency of key information.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly updating the Product Backlog based on feedback.
explanation1: Correct: Keeping the Product Backlog current ensures everyone understands the most valuable and up-to-date work items.
answer2: Conducting frequent Sprint Reviews with stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: Sprint Reviews provide transparency about the Increment and gather valuable feedback.
answer3: Using a visible Task Board to track progress in real-time.
explanation3: Correct: A Task Board helps the team and stakeholders see the status of work, enhancing visibility and communication.
answer4: Skipping Daily Scrums if progress is on track.
explanation4: Incorrect: Daily Scrums are essential for maintaining transparency and should not be skipped.
answer5: Limiting communication to only planned meetings.
explanation5: Incorrect: Effective communication should be ongoing, not limited to formal meetings.

title: During a Daily Scrum, the Developers identify a new risk that might impact the Sprint Goal. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the discussion, helping the Developers find the best approach to address the risk while keeping focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Direct the team on how to handle the risk immediately.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not dictate how the team manages risks.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the team decide the best approach to manage the risk.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master facilitates the team's decision-making process, enabling them to handle risks effectively.
answer3: Ignore the risk to maintain focus on the current plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Risks should be addressed promptly to avoid impacting the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Goal to accommodate the risk.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjusting the Sprint Goal should be a last resort; the team should first explore ways to manage the risk.

title: The Scrum Master observes that the team is not using the Daily Scrum effectively. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the team on using the Daily Scrum effectively, helping them to inspect progress and adapt their work plan as necessary. “The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and that attendees understand its purpose.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Take over the Daily Scrum to ensure it is run correctly.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not lead the Daily Scrum.
answer2: Coach the team on how to use the Daily Scrum to inspect and adapt their progress toward the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should guide the team to optimize the Daily Scrum to support their self-management.
answer3: Ignore the issue to respect the team's autonomy.
explanation3: Incorrect: Providing guidance is part of the Scrum Master’s role, especially when team practices can be improved.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to attend and observe the Daily Scrum.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers; involvement of others should only add value.

title: True or False: The Developers are responsible for ensuring that the Product Backlog is refined. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Refinement is led by the Product Owner but involves the entire Scrum Team, particularly the Developers, to ensure items are actionable. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Product Backlog refinement is a collaborative effort led by the Product Owner, with Developers involved.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner leads the refinement process, ensuring items are clear and ready for the team.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must be available to answer questions about Product Backlog items during the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner plays a key role in clarifying Product Backlog items and should be available to support the Developers throughout the Sprint. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner should be available to clarify items, ensuring the team understands what needs to be delivered.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s availability is crucial to ensuring that the team has the information needed to work efficiently.

title: Which two strategies should the Product Owner use when prioritizing the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Effective prioritization involves balancing value, urgency, and strategic alignment, with the Product Owner making informed decisions to guide the Scrum Team. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Prioritize based solely on stakeholder requests.
explanation1: Incorrect: While stakeholder input is valuable, prioritization must also consider business value, risk, and strategic alignment.
answer2: Order items by potential business value to maximize impact.
explanation2: Correct: Prioritizing by business value ensures the most impactful work is completed first.
answer3: Consider the cost of delay when ordering items.
explanation3: Correct: The cost of delay helps determine which items are most urgent and important to complete.
answer4: Delegate prioritization to the team for technical decisions.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing the Backlog based on overall value, not technical decisions.
answer5: Focus on completing low-effort items first for quick wins.
explanation5: Incorrect: Prioritizing low-effort items does not necessarily align with maximizing value.

title: Which two actions should the Scrum Master take if the Product Owner struggles to prioritize the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master can support the Product Owner by providing guidance and facilitating stakeholder feedback, helping to improve prioritization. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Offer guidance on value-based prioritization techniques.
explanation1: Correct: The Scrum Master can coach the Product Owner on effective prioritization.
answer2: Take over prioritization temporarily.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should not perform the Product Owner's responsibilities.
answer3: Facilitate stakeholder feedback sessions to gather more insights.
explanation3: Correct: Gathering feedback can help the Product Owner make informed prioritization decisions.
answer4: Propose to reduce the Product Backlog size to make prioritization easier.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reducing backlog size does not address the core prioritization challenge.
answer5: Have the Developers take over the prioritization.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner should remain accountable for prioritization decisions.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to keep the Product Backlog relevant and aligned with business needs? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders regularly and use data-driven prioritization to ensure the Product Backlog remains aligned with evolving business needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Update the Product Backlog only during Sprint Planning and Review sessions.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously refined and updated based on evolving needs.
answer2: Engage regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure alignment with business priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement ensures that the Backlog remains relevant and responsive to current needs.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on items that deliver the most value.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help keep the Product Backlog aligned with business objectives and priorities.
answer4: Ignore feedback that does not align with the current Product Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to maintain an adaptable and responsive Product Backlog.
answer5: Delegate Backlog refinement to the Developers to streamline updates.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: Which three techniques can a Product Owner use to maximize value delivery from the Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maximizing value requires the Product Owner to actively manage the Product Backlog using feedback, collaboration, and market analysis to prioritize the most valuable work. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ordering the Product Backlog solely based on stakeholder requests.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ordering should consider value, risk, and other factors, not just stakeholder requests.
answer2: Using feedback from Sprint Reviews to adjust priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Feedback helps ensure the Product Backlog reflects the latest value opportunities.
answer3: Collaborating with the team during refinement sessions to clarify items.
explanation3: Correct: Regular refinement ensures that Product Backlog items are well understood and actionable.
answer4: Delegating prioritization to the Scrum Master.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritization, which cannot be delegated.
answer5: Analyzing market trends and adjusting the Backlog accordingly.
explanation5: Correct: Keeping the Backlog aligned with market needs helps maximize value.

title: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product. Which three activities best help them achieve this? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maximizing value involves prioritizing the Backlog effectively, refining it regularly, and using feedback to adjust goals. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ordering the Product Backlog based on ROI.
explanation1: Correct: Ordering the Backlog by ROI helps prioritize items that bring the most value.
answer2: Spending more time with stakeholders than with the Scrum Team.
explanation2: Incorrect: Balancing engagement with stakeholders and the team is key, not prioritizing one over the other.
answer3: Refining Product Backlog Items regularly with the Scrum Team.
explanation3: Correct: Regular refinement ensures the Backlog is clear and aligned with the value goals.
answer4: Delegating prioritization to the Scrum Master.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner must retain accountability for ordering the Backlog.
answer5: Using customer feedback to guide Backlog adjustments.
explanation5: Correct: Feedback is crucial for aligning the product with market needs and maximizing value.

title: Which action best demonstrates the Product Owner's commitment to maximizing value? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Maximizing value requires continuous engagement with the Product Backlog, using feedback and new information to keep it aligned with stakeholder needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly reprioritizing the Product Backlog based on new insights.
explanation1: Correct: Reprioritizing the Backlog ensures the highest value work is always prioritized, reflecting the latest insights and feedback.
answer2: Delegating Backlog refinement tasks to the Scrum Master.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is directly responsible for Backlog management and cannot delegate this task.
answer3: Focusing only on items that have already been committed.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner must look ahead and prepare the Backlog for future Sprints.
answer4: Only adjusting the Backlog at Sprint Planning.
explanation4: Incorrect: Continuous refinement, not just planning, is necessary to keep the Backlog aligned with value goals.

title: During a Sprint, the team identifies that a Backlog item is more complex than initially thought. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine or split complex items, ensuring they are manageable and aligned with the Sprint Goal. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Encourage the team to complete the item as planned to avoid disruptions.
explanation1: Incorrect: Pushing the team to complete complex work without adjustments can reduce quality and alignment with the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item further or split it into smaller, manageable tasks.
explanation2: Correct: Refining or splitting complex items helps ensure they are achievable within the Sprint’s context.
answer3: Ignore the issue and let the team handle it on their own.
explanation3: Incorrect: Collaboration ensures the team remains aligned and focused on delivering value despite complexity.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to facilitate a separate session to address the issue.
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master can facilitate discussions, the Product Owner should actively engage in refinement efforts.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team highlights ongoing issues with the clarity of Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to improve refinement processes, ensuring that Product Backlog items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Maintain the current refinement process and hope for improvement over time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Continuing without change does not address the root causes of recurring issues.
answer2: Work with the team to enhance the refinement process, ensuring items are clear and understood.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement helps ensure that Product Backlog items are actionable and align with team understanding.
answer3: Delegate the responsibility of refinement to the Scrum Master.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refining Backlog items and must actively participate.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement should be continuously improved, not delayed.

title: True or False: The Product Owner can delegate prioritization of the Product Backlog to the Scrum Master if necessary. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Prioritizing the Product Backlog is a non-delegable responsibility of the Product Owner. Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Prioritization is the core responsibility of the Product Owner and cannot be delegated.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner is solely accountable for prioritizing the Product Backlog.

title: True or False: The Developers are responsible for determining how the Product Backlog items are implemented during the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers are responsible for planning their work during the Sprint and deciding how to achieve the Sprint Goal. “The Developers plan the work necessary to create an Increment that meets the Definition of Done.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Developers decide how to turn Product Backlog items into a usable Increment.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Developers are self-managing and determine their approach during the Sprint.

title: Which two strategies can the Product Owner use to maximize the value of the product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes product value by engaging stakeholders for feedback and prioritizing backlog items based on their potential impact and value. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly engaging with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust priorities.
explanation1: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures the Product Backlog reflects current market and stakeholder needs, maximizing value.
answer2: Prioritizing items based on potential impact and business value.
explanation2: Correct: Focusing on high-value items ensures that the most impactful work is completed first.
answer3: Delegating backlog prioritization to the Development Team.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for backlog prioritization to ensure value is maximized.
answer4: Keeping the backlog static once the Sprint begins.
explanation4: Incorrect: The backlog should be dynamic, adjusting to new insights and feedback as needed.
answer5: Prioritizing technical tasks over business requirements.
explanation5: Incorrect: Technical tasks are important but must align with delivering business value.

title: Which three factors are essential for creating a productive and collaborative environment in a Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Openness, respect, and regular feedback are key elements that help create a productive and collaborative environment within a Scrum Team. “Scrum Teams are cross-functional, self-managing, and have all the skills needed to create value each Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Openness and respect among team members
explanation1: Correct: Openness and respect are critical for effective communication and collaboration within the team.
answer2: A clear Definition of Done
explanation2: Correct: A clear Definition of Done ensures that everyone understands what needs to be achieved for work to be considered complete.
answer3: Regular feedback from stakeholders
explanation3: Correct: Regular feedback helps the team stay aligned with expectations and adapt as needed.
answer4: A command-and-control management style
explanation4: Incorrect: Scrum encourages self-management and autonomy rather than command-and-control approaches.
answer5: Frequent changes to team composition
explanation5: Incorrect: Stability in team composition fosters better collaboration and productivity.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to ensure the Development Team understands the requirements of the Product Backlog items? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner ensures that the Development Team understands the Product Backlog items by participating in refinement sessions and maintaining regular communication. “The Product Owner is accountable for ensuring that the Product Backlog is understood by the Development Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Participate actively in Backlog Refinement sessions.
explanation1: Correct: Active participation helps clarify requirements, ensuring that the team understands what needs to be developed.
answer2: Provide detailed documentation for each item.
explanation2: Incorrect: Detailed documentation can help but should not replace direct communication and collaboration.
answer3: Review requirements only during Sprint Planning.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reviewing requirements solely during Sprint Planning can lead to misunderstandings and delays.
answer4: Engage in frequent communication with the Development Team.
explanation4: Correct: Regular communication ensures that any questions are answered and that the team remains aligned with the Product Owner’s expectations.
answer5: Approve tasks before the team begins work.
explanation5: Incorrect: Approval of tasks is not part of the Product Owner’s role; they ensure clarity but do not approve individual tasks.

title: The Product Owner notices that the Developers are frequently unable to complete their committed work. What should be the first step? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to identify impediments and collaborate on solutions, ensuring the team can meet their commitments. “The Scrum Team identifies the most helpful changes to improve its effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adjust the team's capacity estimates without consulting them.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adjusting estimates without team input does not address the root causes of issues.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the Developers to identify impediments affecting their progress.
explanation2: Correct: Engaging the team helps identify obstacles and fosters a collaborative approach to solving them.
answer3: Reassign incomplete work to the next Sprint automatically.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reassigning work without refinement can lead to repeated failures.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to intervene and manage the Developers' workload.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should work with the team to address issues collaboratively, not delegate responsibility.

title: A new Product Owner is taking over a project mid-Sprint. What is the best approach to ensure a smooth transition? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: A new Product Owner should first observe and understand the current Sprint before making any changes to ensure continuity and informed decision-making. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately review and change the Product Backlog to reflect personal preferences.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sudden changes can disrupt the ongoing work and team focus.
answer2: First observe the current Sprint and learn the existing priorities and team dynamics.
explanation2: Correct: Understanding the current state allows the new Product Owner to make informed decisions going forward.
answer3: Cancel the current Sprint to start fresh with new priorities.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is unnecessary and disruptive.
answer4: Schedule a meeting with stakeholders to redefine goals immediately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Immediate changes should be avoided; focus first on learning the current state.

title: True or False: The Definition of Done is solely created and maintained by the Product Owner. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done is a shared agreement within the Scrum Team, defining what must be completed for work to be considered finished. “The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team collectively, not solely by the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done is established and maintained by the entire Scrum Team to ensure shared understanding of work quality.

title: Which three actions help the Scrum Team maintain alignment with stakeholders throughout the Sprint? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Regular Sprint Reviews, updating the Product Backlog with feedback, and engaging stakeholders during Refinement help maintain strong alignment between the team and stakeholders. “The Scrum Team and stakeholders review what was accomplished in the Sprint Review.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Conducting regular Sprint Reviews with stakeholder participation.
explanation1: Correct: Sprint Reviews allow stakeholders to see progress and provide feedback, ensuring alignment.
answer2: Updating the Product Backlog based on stakeholder feedback after each Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Keeping the Product Backlog current with stakeholder input ensures the team works on the most valuable items.
answer3: Engaging stakeholders in Backlog Refinement sessions.
explanation3: Correct: Involving stakeholders in Refinement ensures that their needs are understood and reflected in upcoming work.
answer4: Sharing daily updates directly with stakeholders.
explanation4: Incorrect: Direct daily updates are not required; formal feedback channels like Sprint Reviews are more effective.
answer5: Inviting stakeholders to the Daily Scrum.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for the Development Team only; other events serve for stakeholder interaction.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when the team consistently misses the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to understand challenges and refine Backlog items, ensuring quality standards are consistently met. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adjust the Definition of Done to lower quality standards.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards compromises the integrity of the product and does not address the root issues.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to understand obstacles and refine the Backlog items.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration helps identify and address obstacles, ensuring that items meet the Definition of Done.
answer3: Reassign incomplete work to the next Sprint without refinement.
explanation3: Incorrect: Moving work forward without addressing issues can lead to repeated failures.
answer4: Improve refinement practices to ensure items are better understood and actionable.
explanation4: Correct: Effective refinement helps ensure that items are clear, manageable, and meet the Definition of Done.
answer5: Ignore the issue as long as some value is delivered.
explanation5: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues undermines the product’s value and consistency.

title: During a Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that their Definition of Done is unclear and causing misunderstandings. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Scrum Team to clarify and update the Definition of Done, ensuring it is well-understood and consistently applied. “The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Wait until the next Sprint to address the issues with the Definition of Done.
explanation1: Incorrect: Delaying improvements can lead to ongoing misunderstandings and inconsistent quality.
answer2: Collaborate with the team immediately to clarify and update the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Updating the Definition of Done helps ensure a shared understanding and consistent quality standards.
answer3: Ignore the issue as it primarily concerns the Developers.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team and should actively contribute to refining the Definition of Done.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to take charge of updating the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is created and maintained by the entire Scrum Team, not just the Scrum Master.

title: Which artifact best represents the ‘inspection’ aspect of the Scrum pillars? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment represents the inspected work completed during the Sprint, allowing the team to review what has been achieved and make necessary adaptations. “The Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog represents work planned for the Sprint but is not the main artifact for inspection.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment is the result of work completed during the Sprint, providing a basis for inspection during the Sprint Review.
answer3: Product Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog outlines future work but does not directly support the inspection pillar.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not directly facilitate inspection.

title: Which artifact provides visibility into the work completed and helps the team track progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment shows completed work and serves as a stepping stone toward achieving the Product Goal, demonstrating progress to the team and stakeholders. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows the plan for the current Sprint but does not track progress toward the Product Goal.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment reflects completed work that moves the product closer to the Product Goal.
answer3: Product Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists future work and priorities but does not directly show completed progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not provide a view of completed work.

title: True or False: The Daily Scrum is used by the Development Team to review their progress and make adjustments to their plan as needed. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum provides a daily opportunity for the Development Team to inspect their progress and adjust their plan, keeping their focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want, as long as their Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum is a daily event where the Development Team inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapts their work plan as necessary.
explanation2: Incorrect: The primary purpose of the Daily Scrum is for the Development Team to inspect and adapt their progress toward the Sprint Goal.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must attend every Daily Scrum to ensure the team is working on the most important tasks. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum is a meeting for the Development Team to inspect their progress and adapt as needed, without mandatory attendance from the Product Owner. “The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not need to attend the Daily Scrum; this event is for the Development Team to inspect and adapt their plan.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is for the Development Team, and while the Product Owner can attend, it is not mandatory for their role.

title: Which three activities should the Development Team focus on during Sprint Planning? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: During Sprint Planning, the Development Team focuses on defining how to achieve the Sprint Goal, identifying tasks, and discussing potential risks to ensure a successful Sprint. “Sprint Planning answers the following: What can be Done this Sprint? How will the chosen work get done?” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defining how they will achieve the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Correct: Planning how to achieve the Sprint Goal sets the foundation for the Sprint’s work.
answer2: Identifying the tasks needed to complete the selected Product Backlog items.
explanation2: Correct: Breaking down selected items into actionable tasks helps the team understand the work ahead.
answer3: Establishing a detailed timeline for each task.
explanation3: Incorrect: Scrum emphasizes flexibility and does not require detailed timelines for tasks.
answer4: Discussing potential risks and how to mitigate them.
explanation4: Correct: Identifying risks allows the team to proactively address challenges that may impact the Sprint.
answer5: Assigning specific tasks to individuals based on skills.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Development Team self-organizes and decides who will work on which tasks during the Sprint.

title: Which two events provide formal opportunities to inspect and adapt the product and the process? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective are key opportunities for the Scrum Team to inspect their product and processes and make necessary adaptations. “Scrum is a framework that enables teams to inspect and adapt at frequent intervals.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Review
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Review inspects the product.
answer2: Sprint Retrospective
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint retrospective inspect the process.
answer3: Definition of Done
explanation3: Incorrect: Definition of Done sets quality criteria but are not formal events.
answer4: Sprint Planning
explanation4: Incorrect: This event is for planning, not formal adaptation of the product and process.
answer5: Increment
explanation5: Incorrect: This is an artifact, not event for inspection and adaptation.

title: What is the primary focus of the Product Owner during the Sprint Review? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is an opportunity for the Product Owner to gather feedback on the Increment and adjust future plans accordingly. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: To assess the team's performance during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is not focused on performance assessment.
answer2: To present the Increment and gather feedback from stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner's main role is to facilitate feedback on the Increment to guide future Backlog refinements.
answer3: To update the stakeholders on the progress of the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: The focus is on the Increment, not on the backlog updates.
answer4: To decide which items will be in the next Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Planning the next Sprint happens during Sprint Planning, not the Review.

title: The Development Team finds that they often need to rework tasks because they did not fully understand the requirements. Which Scrum event should they focus on improving to address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Backlog Refinement sessions help the team understand requirements better, reducing the need for rework by ensuring clarity before tasks are started. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Review
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is for inspecting the Increment and gathering feedback, not for clarifying future work requirements.
answer2: Backlog Refinement
explanation2: Correct: Backlog Refinement helps ensure that requirements are clear and well understood before they are pulled into a Sprint, reducing the need for rework.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for inspecting progress during the Sprint, not for clarifying task requirements.
answer4: Sprint Retrospective
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective focuses on process improvement rather than clarifying requirements for tasks.

title: The team is having difficulty completing the tasks defined in their Sprint Backlog. What action should they take to improve their future Sprints? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Retrospective is a key event for the team to inspect what went well, what didn’t, and plan changes to improve their effectiveness in future Sprints. “The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint by planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Increase the length of their Sprints to give them more time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint length is not allowed in Scrum and does not address the underlying issues of task completion.
answer2: Use the Sprint Retrospective to identify and address the reasons for incomplete tasks.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective is designed to identify areas for improvement and plan actions to enhance future performance.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to manage their workload better.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Development Team is self-managing and responsible for organizing their work.
answer4: Reallocate tasks to team members who are less busy.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reallocating tasks does not resolve systemic issues and may disrupt the team’s flow.

title: Which pillar of Scrum enables the team to assess and address variances between expected and actual outcomes? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Inspection enables the team to assess and address variances, ensuring that progress toward goals is continually evaluated and managed. “Inspection without adaptation is considered pointless.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Correct: Inspection allows the team to assess progress and identify variances that need to be addressed.
answer2: Adaptation
explanation2: Incorrect: Adaptation occurs after Inspection has identified variances.
answer3: Transparency
explanation3: Incorrect: Transparency makes variances visible but does not directly assess them.
answer4: Respect
explanation4: Incorrect: Respect supports positive interactions but does not involve assessing outcomes.

title: Which three pillars of Scrum are demonstrated when the Scrum Team inspects and adapts their work during the Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The pillars of Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation enable the team to continuously improve their processes and adapt based on observations. “Scrum relies on three pillars: transparency, inspection, and adaptation.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Correct: Inspection helps the team identify areas for improvement in their work process.
answer2: Transparency
explanation2: Correct: Transparency allows the team to openly discuss what went well and what could be improved.
answer3: Respect
explanation3: Incorrect: While a value, Respect is not one of the three pillars that directly facilitate process improvement.
answer4: Adaptation
explanation4: Correct: Adaptation allows the team to adjust their process based on their inspections.
answer5: Focus
explanation5: Incorrect: Focus is a Scrum value, not a pillar related to process inspection and adaptation.

title: Which three practices help ensure the Scrum Team delivers work that meets stakeholder expectations? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Engaging stakeholders, using a clear Definition of Done, and prioritizing items based on stakeholder input help ensure the Scrum Team delivers valuable and expected results. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Engaging stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback.
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Review provides a critical opportunity to gather feedback and ensure alignment with stakeholder expectations.
answer2: Using a clear Definition of Done to maintain quality standards.
explanation2: Correct: A well-defined Definition of Done ensures that the work delivered meets agreed quality criteria.
answer3: Prioritizing Product Backlog items based on stakeholder input.
explanation3: Correct: Prioritizing based on input helps align the work with stakeholder needs and expectations.
answer4: Skipping the Retrospective to focus on more development work.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective is essential for continuous improvement and ensuring that the team’s processes align with stakeholder needs.
answer5: Only communicating with stakeholders at the end of the project.
explanation5: Incorrect: Ongoing communication with stakeholders is necessary to ensure their expectations are met throughout the project.

title: Which two tools or techniques can help the Scrum Team track their progress during the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Using the Burndown Chart and Task Board helps the Scrum Team visualize their progress during the Sprint, allowing for adjustments and alignment with the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum artifacts are designed to maximize transparency of key information.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Burndown Chart
explanation1: Correct: The Burndown Chart visually represents the amount of work remaining, helping the team track their progress towards the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Task Board
explanation2: Correct: A Task Board provides a clear visual of tasks in progress, completed, and yet to start, aiding in tracking Sprint progress.
answer3: Velocity Tracking
explanation3: Incorrect: Velocity Tracking helps in planning future Sprints but does not directly track current progress.
answer4: Sprint Review
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Review inspects completed work but does not track progress during the Sprint.
answer5: Daily Scrum
explanation5: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum inspects progress but is not a tool; it’s a meeting that facilitates tracking.

title: A team notices that their Sprint Planning sessions are often running longer than necessary. Which tool or technique could help them streamline this process? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Timeboxing ensures that meetings like Sprint Planning do not exceed their intended duration, keeping the team focused and efficient. “Time-boxing is a key tool to manage effort and efficiency in Scrum.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Timeboxing
explanation1: Correct: Timeboxing limits the duration of meetings, helping the team stay focused and efficient during Sprint Planning.
answer2: Burndown Chart
explanation2: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress but does not directly influence meeting length.
answer3: Retrospective
explanation3: Incorrect: Retrospectives address broader team improvements, not specifically meeting durations.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures task quality but does not manage meeting length.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team is struggling to decide how much work to commit to. Which tool can help them make this decision? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Velocity Tracking provides insights into the team’s past performance, allowing them to make informed decisions about how much work to commit to in the Sprint. “Velocity is an optional but useful tool to help understand team performance.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Burndown Chart
explanation1: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress within a Sprint but does not help with planning capacity.
answer2: Velocity Tracking
explanation2: Correct: Velocity Tracking helps the team understand their historical capacity, aiding in setting realistic commitments during Sprint Planning.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum helps inspect progress but does not assist with Sprint Planning.
answer4: Product Backlog
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists all work but does not specifically help with capacity planning.

title: The Product Owner often requests additional tasks during the Sprint, leading to constant adjustments. Which Scrum tool can help maintain focus on the Sprint Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog helps the Scrum Team maintain focus by clearly defining the tasks committed for the Sprint, preventing scope creep and preserving the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog makes visible all the work that the Developers identify as necessary to meet the Sprint Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog manages future work but does not enforce current Sprint boundaries.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog clearly defines the work committed for the Sprint and helps maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Sprint Review
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Review focuses on completed work, not managing changes during the Sprint.
answer4: Daily Scrum
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum helps inspect progress but does not manage scope changes directly.

title: Which tool or technique helps Scrum Teams forecast their capacity and plan the right amount of work for a Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Velocity Tracking helps teams forecast their capacity based on past performance, allowing for more accurate Sprint Planning and workload management. “Velocity is an optional but useful tool to help understand team performance.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Burndown Chart
explanation1: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks work during the Sprint but does not forecast capacity for planning.
answer2: Velocity Tracking
explanation2: Correct: Velocity Tracking allows teams to measure their past performance, helping them estimate how much work they can handle in future Sprints.
answer3: Scrum Artifacts
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality standards but does not help with capacity planning.
answer4: Daily Scrum
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum inspects progress but does not help with Sprint capacity planning.

title: Which Scrum value is most emphasized when the team discusses openly what is working well and what isn’t during a Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Openness is crucial in the Sprint Retrospective, enabling honest discussions about successes and areas for improvement. “The Scrum Team and its stakeholders are open about the work and the challenges.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Commitment
explanation1: Incorrect: Commitment drives dedication, but openness is key in retrospectives.
answer2: Openness
explanation2: Correct: Openness is emphasized during Retrospectives as it allows the team to discuss challenges honestly and transparently.
answer3: Respect
explanation3: Incorrect: Respect is crucial but does not directly drive open discussion about team performance.
answer4: Focus
explanation4: Incorrect: Focus keeps the team on track, but Retrospectives require openness for honest dialogue.

title: True or False: The Developers are responsible for defining the Sprint Goal during Sprint Planning. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal is established by the Scrum Team, including the Developers, Scrum Master, and Product Owner, ensuring alignment and shared objectives. “The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is a collaborative effort defined by the entire Scrum Team, including the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal is defined collaboratively by the Scrum Team during Sprint Planning.

title: True or False: The Product Owner should cancel the Sprint if the Developers identify an issue that makes the Sprint Goal unattainable. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner can cancel a Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but this action is not mandatory and should be carefully considered. “A Sprint can be canceled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is a decision that should be made carefully, considering all factors, not just the immediate issue.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner may cancel the Sprint if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, but it is not mandatory.

title: During a Sprint Planning session, the team expresses concern that they might not complete all selected items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the Sprint remains focused on delivering the most valuable work within capacity. “The Sprint Backlog is composed of the Sprint Goal (why), the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what), and an actionable plan for delivering the Increment (how).” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Encourage the team to push through and complete all items regardless of challenges.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint Planning should focus on realistic commitments, not pushing beyond capacity.
answer2: Work with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog to focus on the most valuable items.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps ensure the team can deliver valuable work within the Sprint.
answer3: Ask the team to work extra hours to meet the Sprint commitment.
explanation3: Incorrect: Overworking the team is not a sustainable approach and contradicts Scrum principles.
answer4: Cancel the Sprint and restart with fewer items.
explanation4: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is an extreme measure and should be used sparingly.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers express that the selected items may exceed their capacity. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the team commits to achievable and valuable work. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Push the team to commit to the selected work to meet deadlines.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to incomplete work and team burnout.
answer2: Work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on the highest value items.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog ensures commitments are achievable and aligned with delivering value.
answer3: Ignore the concerns and proceed with the original plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Addressing capacity concerns helps maintain team morale and productivity.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to facilitate a discussion on workload management.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should actively participate in managing work scope and priorities with the team.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner requests to change a priority in the Product Backlog. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog can be adjusted anytime, but changes to the Sprint Backlog should be avoided mid-Sprint. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately adjust the Sprint Backlog to reflect the change.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes to the Sprint Backlog should be avoided during the Sprint.
answer2: Discuss the change in the next Daily Scrum and adjust accordingly.
explanation2: Incorrect: Daily Scrum is not intended for backlog adjustments.
answer3: Continue the current Sprint as planned and adjust in the next Sprint Planning.
explanation3: Correct: The Sprint Goal should remain stable during a Sprint; adjustments happen in the next planning session.
answer4: Cancel the current Sprint and start a new one with the updated priorities.
explanation4: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is a disruptive approach that should only be used in extreme cases.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers raise concerns about the feasibility of completing all the selected Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to refine and adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the Sprint Goal remains achievable and focused on delivering value. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Insist that all items are completed to maintain the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: Forcing unrealistic commitments can lead to unmet goals and lower team morale.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on the most valuable items.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps align the team’s capacity with achievable work while maintaining focus on value.
answer3: Delay the Sprint to reevaluate the work items and Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying a Sprint disrupts the flow of work and is not aligned with Scrum principles.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to resolve the team’s concerns independently.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should actively participate in addressing concerns during Sprint Planning.

title: During a Sprint Review, stakeholders express concern that the Increment does not meet their needs. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and refine the Product Backlog, ensuring it aligns with their needs. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the Increment and explain the team’s efforts.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending work without addressing feedback does not help improve the product.
answer2: Engage stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage stakeholder feedback and update the Backlog to reflect their needs.
answer3: Ignore the feedback to avoid disrupting future Sprints.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can lead to misalignment and missed opportunities.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle stakeholder feedback.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing feedback and adjusting the Product Backlog is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders express that the Increment does not meet their needs. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage with stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and update the Product Backlog, ensuring future work aligns with their needs. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the Increment by explaining the challenges faced by the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending the work without action does not address stakeholder concerns or improve the product.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage stakeholder feedback and refine the Product Backlog to better align with their needs.
answer3: Ignore the feedback to maintain the current Product Backlog priorities.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of the Sprint Review and stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle stakeholder feedback.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder feedback and expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: A stakeholder complains that their feedback was not reflected in the last Increment. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog as necessary to ensure future work aligns with their needs. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Explain that the team is focused on other priorities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Dismissing feedback can harm stakeholder relationships and trust.
answer2: Engage the stakeholder to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should manage stakeholder feedback and ensure it is considered in future Backlog prioritization.
answer3: Ignore the feedback if it does not align with the current Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Product Backlog aligned with stakeholder needs.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the stakeholder’s expectations.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing stakeholder feedback and expectations.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the role of the Product Owner in managing stakeholder expectations? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner effectively manages stakeholder expectations by engaging regularly, using data to explain decisions, and setting clear boundaries on achievable work. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only communicating with stakeholders during formal Scrum events.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ongoing communication is essential for managing expectations and aligning the Product Backlog with stakeholder needs.
answer2: Regularly engaging stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement ensures the Backlog remains aligned with current needs and business objectives.
answer3: Using metrics to provide transparency on prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven insights help stakeholders understand why certain items are prioritized, building trust.
answer4: Setting clear expectations about what can and cannot be achieved within the current Sprint.
explanation4: Correct: Transparent communication helps stakeholders understand the scope and focus of the Sprint.
answer5: Delegating stakeholder management to the Scrum Master to avoid disruptions.
explanation5: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder expectations is a key responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers find that a key task is blocking progress on other work. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to address and prioritize the removal of blockers, ensuring the team can maintain progress towards the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by removing impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the issue and let the Developers handle it on their own.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring impediments can lead to delays and failure to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Collaborate with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on removing the blocker.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should support the team in prioritizing the resolution of blockers to maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to solve the problem for the team.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not solve issues directly for the team.
answer4: Remove the task from the Sprint Backlog to avoid further delays.
explanation4: Incorrect: Removing work without resolving the issue does not address the underlying problem.

title: Which concept is most closely related to the idea that Scrum Teams are self-managing and decide who does what, when, and how? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Self-organization is a core principle of Scrum, empowering teams to manage their work independently and make decisions collectively. “Self-managing teams choose who, how, and when their work gets done.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Timeboxing
explanation1: Incorrect: Timeboxing is about limiting the duration of Scrum events, not about self-management.
answer2: Self-organization
explanation2: Correct: Self-organization empowers Scrum Teams to manage their own work without external control.
answer3: Cross-functionality
explanation3: Incorrect: Cross-functionality refers to having all the skills needed in the team, not decision-making autonomy.
answer4: Transparency
explanation4: Incorrect: Transparency relates to making work visible but does not directly involve self-management.

title: During a Sprint, a key stakeholder requests a high-priority change. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate the stakeholder’s request and manage it through the Product Backlog, ensuring the current Sprint remains focused. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the change immediately to keep the stakeholder satisfied.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding new work mid-Sprint disrupts the focus and may jeopardize the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the change and prioritize it in the Product Backlog for future consideration.
explanation2: Correct: Managing changes through the Product Backlog allows the team to maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Reject the request to avoid disrupting the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback should be considered, even if not actionable immediately.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the stakeholder’s expectations.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing stakeholder feedback and the Product Backlog.

title: During Sprint Review, stakeholders request changes that could alter the Product Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should assess feedback collaboratively with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to determine the impact on the Product Goal and Backlog. “The Product Owner is responsible for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately change the Product Goal to align with stakeholder requests.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing the Product Goal without evaluation can disrupt the product’s strategic direction.
answer2: Discuss the feedback with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to assess the impact on the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should collaborate to evaluate changes and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
answer3: Reject the changes to keep the current focus intact.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered and evaluated thoughtfully.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage stakeholder expectations.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the Product Goal and stakeholder feedback.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies repeated delays due to unclear requirements. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to improve refinement practices, ensuring that requirements are clear and actionable to prevent future delays. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and maintain the current refinement practices.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring issues in refinement can lead to ongoing inefficiencies and misunderstandings.
answer2: Improve refinement practices with the team to ensure requirements are clear and well understood.
explanation2: Correct: Enhancing refinement helps reduce delays caused by unclear Product Backlog items.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the refinement process separately.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and should actively participate in improvements.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be ongoing and not delayed until formal planning sessions.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner receives feedback that a key feature does not meet user expectations. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate feedback and work with the team to adjust the Product Backlog, ensuring that the product evolves to meet user expectations. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback to maintain focus on the current Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can result in misalignment with user needs and reduced product value.
answer2: Assess the feedback, discuss it with the team, and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should evaluate feedback and update the Product Backlog to reflect user needs.
answer3: Immediately stop the current Sprint and adjust the feature.
explanation3: Incorrect: Stopping a Sprint disrupts progress and should only be done if the Sprint Goal is no longer valuable.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the feedback and make the necessary changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing feedback and adjusting the Product Backlog is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: Which two actions demonstrate a Product Owner effectively managing the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Effective Product Owners continuously refine the Backlog and communicate changes clearly to the team to ensure alignment and readiness. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Prioritizing Backlog items based on stakeholder requests alone.
explanation1: Incorrect: Prioritization should balance stakeholder input with value and feasibility.
answer2: Refining Product Backlog items regularly to ensure they are clear and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous refinement helps keep the Backlog ready for future Sprints.
answer3: Allowing the team to decide which items to prioritize.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for prioritization decisions.
answer4: Communicating changes in prioritization to the team in a timely manner.
explanation4: Correct: Keeping the team informed helps maintain alignment on priorities.
answer5: Reviewing the Backlog only at the end of each Sprint.
explanation5: Incorrect: Regular review is essential for an up-to-date Backlog.

title: Which three actions demonstrate effective Product Backlog management by the Product Owner? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Product Backlog management involves continuous refinement, prioritization based on feedback and data, and collaboration with the team to ensure the Backlog reflects current needs and goals. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delegating all refinement tasks to the Scrum Master to save time.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the Product Backlog and cannot delegate this responsibility entirely.
answer2: Regularly reprioritizing items based on stakeholder feedback and market trends.
explanation2: Correct: Reprioritizing the Backlog ensures it reflects current priorities and delivers maximum value.
answer3: Collaborating with the Developers to clarify and refine Backlog items continuously.
explanation3: Correct: Ongoing collaboration ensures Backlog items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints.
answer4: Using data and metrics to drive prioritization decisions.
explanation4: Correct: Data-driven prioritization helps align the Product Backlog with business goals and value delivery.
answer5: Waiting until the next Sprint Planning to make adjustments to the Product Backlog.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement and adjustments should be ongoing, not delayed until Sprint Planning.

title: Which action best demonstrates the Product Owner's commitment to maximizing the value of the product? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes product value by continuously engaging with stakeholders and adapting the Product Backlog accordingly. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Frequently reordering the Product Backlog based on daily team feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Reordering the backlog daily may lead to instability and lack of focus.
answer2: Engaging with stakeholders and adjusting the Product Backlog based on their feedback.
explanation2: Correct: Active engagement and adaptation based on feedback ensures the product delivers value.
answer3: Minimizing interactions with stakeholders to focus on internal processes.
explanation3: Incorrect: Limiting stakeholder interaction reduces valuable insights for the product.
answer4: Delegating backlog refinement to the Scrum Master to save time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Backlog refinement is a core responsibility of the Product Owner and cannot be delegated.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Scrum Master's role in supporting the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the Scrum Team by facilitating events, assisting the Product Owner with Backlog refinement, and coaching the team on self-management. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Directing the team on what to work on each day.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not direct the team’s work.
answer2: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive and effective.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating Scrum events is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer3: Helping the Product Owner refine and prioritize the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the Product Owner in managing the Backlog effectively.
answer4: Coaching the team on self-management and cross-functionality.
explanation4: Correct: Coaching the team helps them become more autonomous and effective in their work.
answer5: Assigning tasks to team members to improve efficiency.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks; the team manages their own work.

title: Which artifact helps ensure transparency in the Scrum process by providing a clear plan for what the team will work on during the Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog ensures transparency by showing what the team will work on during the Sprint, providing clear visibility into the planned tasks. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists all future work but does not outline the plan for the current Sprint.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides a transparent view of the team’s work plan during the Sprint.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows completed work but does not outline the current Sprint plan.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not provide a work plan.

title: Which artifact serves as a single source of truth for all work needed to achieve the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is the single source of truth for all work needed to achieve the Product Goal, providing visibility into future tasks and priorities. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog only contains work planned for the current Sprint and does not include all work toward the Product Goal.
answer2: Product Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog contains all items that the Scrum Team may work on to achieve the Product Goal.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment represents completed work but does not list future tasks.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not outline all work toward the Product Goal.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is allowed to add new tasks to the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog is committed during Sprint Planning, and no additional work should be added once the Sprint begins, ensuring focus on the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner cannot add tasks to the Sprint Backlog once the Sprint has started; the team focuses on the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: Once the Sprint starts, the Sprint Backlog is fixed and the Development Team focuses on achieving the Sprint Goal without adding new tasks.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team finds an item that is not fully refined but critical. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine the critical item, ensuring it is ready for inclusion in the current Sprint. This maintains the focus on delivering value without compromising quality. “Product Backlog items that can be Done by the Scrum Team within one Sprint are deemed ready for selection in a Sprint Planning event.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the item as-is to keep the Sprint on track.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including unrefined items can disrupt the Sprint and affect team focus.
answer2: Work with the team to refine the item quickly so it can be included in the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should help refine the item to ensure it is clear and actionable, if it is critical to the Sprint.
answer3: Move the item to the next Sprint to allow more time for refinement.
explanation3: Incorrect: Moving the item could delay important work if it is a high priority.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the refinement process.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement is a collaborative activity involving the Product Owner and the Developers.

title: Which action should the Product Owner take if the Product Backlog is not clearly defined before Sprint Planning? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Even if the Product Backlog is not perfectly refined, the team should plan with what is available and refine as they go. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Refine the Product Backlog during Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint Planning is not meant for refining backlog items.
answer2: Delay the Sprint Planning until the Product Backlog is ready.
explanation2: Incorrect: Delaying events disrupts the team's cadence.
answer3: Work with the team during the Sprint to refine the unclear items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Refinement should happen outside of the Sprint's development time.
answer4: Proceed with the available Product Backlog items and plan the Sprint.
explanation4: Correct: The team should work with what is available, adjusting as necessary.

title: Which three factors help a Scrum Team maintain a high level of transparency in their work? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining a visible Task Board, updating the Product Backlog, and having a clear Definition of Done help the team work transparently and stay aligned. “Transparency enables inspection. Inspection without transparency is misleading and wasteful.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Using a visible Task Board to track progress.
explanation1: Correct: A Task Board provides clear visibility of the team’s work, enhancing transparency.
answer2: Regularly updating the Product Backlog with feedback and changes.
explanation2: Correct: Keeping the Product Backlog updated ensures that everyone understands the priorities and upcoming work.
answer3: Having a Definition of Done that is shared and understood by the entire team.
explanation3: Correct: A clear Definition of Done ensures that quality standards are known and met consistently.
answer4: Completing work without documenting it to save time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Documentation, as needed, supports transparency and shared understanding.
answer5: Keeping meetings to a minimum to focus on work.
explanation5: Incorrect: Effective meetings are essential to maintain communication and transparency among the team.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner’s responsibility for Product Backlog management? (Choose the three best answers)
